question: Is the adaptive repair loop that detects one-hop failures and generates corrective examples practical to implement and likely to converge?
description: Examine iterative reasoning frameworks like KGEIR and see if they use similar repair loops.
rationale: Assess implementation complexity and potential pitfalls.
resolution: Feasibility of the adaptive repair loop is supported by works showing iterative refinement improves performance (IterCOMP, DynaSearcher, CacheRAG). Reinforcement learning lower-hop transfer has been explored in multi-hop KGQA (e.g., the RL-based methods in the analyzed papers), indicating that optimizing on lower-hop QA instances can transfer to deeper multi-hop queries. However, direct evidence combining an adaptive repair loop that detects one-hop failures, generates corrective examples, and then applies RL lower-hop transfer is not present in the literature.
